Title: Historical provider Origin bypass corrected externally during audit
Description: RESOLVED IN FINAL RECHECK, not an open bypass: initial production guard accepted forged localhost Origin without bearer; source changed externally and final isolated recheck rejects with 401. New provider guard tests pass. Deployment of corrected source is UNVERIFIED.
Impact: Unauthenticated modification of all provider-managed companies, licenses and control records.
Likelihood: Not reproduced in final source; deployed version unknown
Recommended fix: Retain the permanent regression matrix and confirm deployed artifact matches corrected guard; complete shared-key identity and secret fixes separately. No guard patch was made by this audit.

Title: Known production secret fallbacks
Description: STILL OPEN 15 OCT: apps/api/src/utils/crypto.ts falls back to a committed encryption key when ENCRYPTION_SECRET is unset. Earlier finding: PARTIALLY CORRECTED EXTERNALLY at 54c5fe9: production compose now requires the tenant JWT secret, provider key and provider JWT secret with no fallback. Rotation evidence and the remaining items below are open. Earlier finding: STATIC, STILL OPEN: production compose retains known provider/tenant/admin key defaults; tenant JWT fallback passes weak-pattern validator. Final provider guard rejects its own development fallback only, not the different compose default. Provider web now includes a shared-key fallback and VITE_ADMIN_API_KEY path.
Impact: Shared credentials and forgeable tokens if operators omit overrides; historical credential exposure cannot be excluded.
Likelihood: High on default deployment
Recommended fix: Require independently generated per-deployment secrets with no fallback; integrate secret delivery and rotation; revoke exposed sessions/keys after deployment inventory.

Title: Provider has no named-user authentication or RBAC
Description: STATIC: ProviderAdmin schema exists but routes rely on one shared bearer and caller-supplied actor; no provider MFA, per-person session lifecycle or role enforcement. Final guard authenticates the shared key and no longer trusts localhost origins.
Impact: No attribution, least privilege, per-user revocation or accountable privileged actions.
Likelihood: Certain design gap
Recommended fix: Implement provider identity and MFA with scoped sessions, operator roles, sensitive-action reauthentication and immutable actor identity.

Title: Provider exposes API and license keys in company responses
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 15 OCT: list, detail and license responses omit apiKey. licenseKey is still returned on every read, and creation returns the enrollment key once by design. Earlier finding: STATIC: getCompanies returns full Company records, including plaintext apiKey/licenseKey, alongside metrics/actions; no response projection or secret lifecycle.
Impact: Mass disclosure of tenant-management credentials and licensing secrets.
Likelihood: High after any shared provider-key exposure
Recommended fix: Use explicit response DTOs, one-time key issuance and hashed credentials where verification suffices; separately encrypt retrievable license material with managed keys.

Title: Sensitive fields remain plaintext at rest
Description: STATIC: license/API/TOTP secrets, GSTIN and payment references have no active field encryption; AES helper is unused and has a known fallback key.
Impact: Database or backup disclosure exposes identity, financial and authentication material.
Likelihood: Medium; deployment encryption UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Classify fields; hash authenticating keys and envelope-encrypt retrievable sensitive values with versioned keys, access controls and rotation migration; define retention/redaction.

Title: Tenant bearer tokens stored in localStorage
Description: STATIC: browser stores token in origin-readable localStorage; XSS can obtain reusable session credentials.
Impact: Session theft and account compromise.
Likelihood: Medium; higher with SEC-008
Recommended fix: Design server-managed Secure HttpOnly SameSite sessions or equivalent protected BFF flow; add CSRF defense for cookie mutations and explicit expiry/revocation handling.

Title: Bearer token placed in health and Studio URLs
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): the embedded API health dashboard and the in-app 404 links that carried the session token to localhost tools are removed; no source under apps or scripts builds a token-bearing URL. Earlier finding: PARTIALLY CORRECTED EXTERNALLY: tenant App links were removed during audit. The API diagnostic HTML still reads browser bearer storage and creates a token-bearing Studio URL; query values may persist in history, logs and referrers.
Impact: Credential leakage to diagnostic surfaces; database tooling exposure.
Likelihood: High for users opening links
Recommended fix: Remove token-bearing URLs; authenticate diagnostics through a scoped session, restrict Studio to approved operator networks and redact historical URL logs.

Title: Unescaped label title reaches document.write
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610122122_P0_Safety): the label print window now escapes the label type and code; the template is a pure function with a regression test (BarcodeQRModal.test.tsx). Earlier finding: STATIC: raw label code is interpolated into a popup HTML title; user-supplied inward batch references are not restricted to safe title content. Browser exploit execution was not performed.
Impact: Stored HTML/script injection can execute in a same-origin print popup.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Use DOM textContent or a safe isolated print document, validate identifiers by domain rules, apply restrictive CSP and sever opener access.

Title: No global or distributed request throttling
Description: STILL OPEN 15 OCT: @nestjs/throttler is a root dependency, but no module registers ThrottlerModule. Earlier finding: STATIC: installed Nest Throttler is not registered; selected public guards use per-process IP maps; protected endpoints and TOTP have no shared per-user/tenant budgets.
Impact: Brute force, resource exhaustion and public-order stock abuse; multiple replicas bypass limits.
Likelihood: High under abuse
Recommended fix: Implement layered gateway and application quotas with shared atomic storage, endpoint-specific limits, verified proxy configuration and lockout observability.

Title: Legacy plaintext passwords accepted
Description: STATIC: login supports plaintext password comparison and upgrades after successful authentication; stored legacy users remain exposed until login.
Impact: Database leak immediately compromises remaining legacy credentials.
Likelihood: Medium; live population UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Inventory affected accounts without exposing passwords, require secure reset/migration, remove plaintext authentication branch and enforce a single password hashing policy.

Title: Password change leaves existing sessions valid
Description: STATIC: self-service password change does not revoke prior sessions; admin reset does. MFA enrollment lacks clear recent-password challenge/replay state.
Impact: A stolen session survives account recovery or enables persistence through new credentials.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Atomically rotate/revoke sessions on password and authenticator changes; require recent strong authentication and audit enrollment/removal with recovery flow.

Title: WebAuthn bound to wrong origin and incomplete MFA flow
Description: STATIC: rpID localhost and origin port 5173 are hardcoded; challenge has no explicit expiry/type record; passkey login re-enters login without the TOTP required for MFA users.
Impact: Production passkeys fail; TOTP-enabled users cannot complete passkey login; challenge lifecycle is weak.
Likelihood: High when enabled
Recommended fix: Configure validated RP/origin per deployment, persist single-use expiring ceremony challenges, and model composed authentication factors with explicit continuation.

Title: Audit trail incomplete and mutable
Description: STATIC: critical invoice/payment/license/settings/machine/jobwork writes lack consistent actor/entity/IP audit entries; dormant AuditService is in-memory; ActivityLog has no tamper-evidence or append-only enforcement.
Impact: Financial and privileged changes cannot be reliably attributed or reconstructed after compromise.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Define domain audit events in the same transaction/outbox as changes; include actor, tenant deployment, entity, before/after digest, IP and correlation ID; enforce append-only retention with independently protected evidence.

Title: Coarse RBAC exposes HR and operational data to all viewers
Description: STATIC: default read permission applies across domains, including personnel/payroll fields; UI navigation restrictions do not implement field-level access policy.
Impact: Staff with generic VIEWER access can read sensitive salary/contact information.
Likelihood: High if low-privilege accounts exist
Recommended fix: Define domain and field permissions with explicit response projections; enforce server-side policy and mirror capabilities in UI.

Title: CSV exports allow formulas and malformed cells
Description: STATIC: csvGenerator only conditionally quotes commas; quotes/newlines are not fully escaped and spreadsheet formula prefixes are unsanitized in exports.
Impact: Opening customer-controlled exported values can execute spreadsheet formulas; data shifts between rows/columns.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Centralize standards-compliant CSV escaping and formula-neutralization policy; offer typed XLSX export where needed.

Title: Public diagnostics disclose operational state and misstate health
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): GET / and GET /health return only service, status, a database flag and time, with 503 when the database is unreachable; operational detail is at GET /status for ADMIN; /api/status and /api/processors are removed. Earlier finding: STATIC: public health/status/processor endpoints expose operational counts; web/Studio states are assumed; degraded DB still returns HTTP 200 and no readiness contract exists.
Impact: Reconnaissance and broken deployment health decisions; false operational confidence.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Separate minimal public liveness from dependency-aware readiness and authenticated diagnostics; return failing readiness status and restrict detail.

Title: Privacy lifecycle not implemented or evidenced
Description: GAP: no complete data inventory, erasure/export/retention policy, geolocation consent basis or backup-erasure strategy was found; legal applicability is UNVERIFIED.
Impact: Uncontrolled PII retention, incomplete customer contractual and legal readiness.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Have privacy/legal owners define applicable obligations; implement scoped export, retention and legally compatible erasure with immutable financial retention exceptions.

Title: No complete history and deployed-secret attestation
Description: GAP: current-source/default and tracked-file scans identify risks; entire historical secret validity, deployed secret stores, image layers and actual client secrets remain UNVERIFIED.
Impact: Previously exposed real credentials could remain usable despite source cleanup.
Likelihood: Unknown
Recommended fix: Run approved redacted history/image/secret-store scans, verify findings with owners, rotate affected credentials and record revocation evidence without committing secret values.

Title: Tenant migration chain does not produce current schema
Description: RESOLVED EXTERNALLY, MEASURED 12 OCT on 54c5fe9: migration 20261012000000_align_system_settings_licensing was added and prisma migrate diff reports no difference on an empty database. Drifted databases remain a risk; see DB-012. Earlier finding: REPRODUCED: all 21 registered SQLite migrations replay, but 14 SystemSettings licensing fields in current Prisma schema are absent from resulting tables.
Impact: Clean deploys fail on settings/license queries; upgraded databases can diverge from code.
Likelihood: Certain from migration chain
Recommended fix: Create reviewed additive migrations with explicit backfill/default policy, production-like upgrade rehearsals and schema-diff gates; preserve business records.

Title: Provider migration chain omits license fields and RemoteAction
Description: RESOLVED EXTERNALLY, MEASURED 12 OCT on 54c5fe9: prisma migrate diff for the provider schema reports no difference on an empty database. Earlier finding: REPRODUCED: 3 registered migrations omit 15 Company fields and the complete RemoteAction table expected by current code.
Impact: Provider company/license/action APIs fail against a freshly migrated database.
Likelihood: Certain from migration chain
Recommended fix: Author versioned additive provider migrations and data backfills; gate releases on clean/populated migration parity and compatible rollout.

Title: PostgreSQL tenant mode is not implemented
Description: STATIC: both Prisma schemas and all registered migrations target SQLite; changing DATABASE_URL to PostgreSQL as suggested in environment comments cannot change provider semantics.
Impact: Large-tenant deployment promise is unsupported; date/decimal/locking/SQL behavior cannot be assumed portable.
Likelihood: Certain feature gap
Recommended fix: Define supported storage profiles with separate generated clients/migration chains or a deliberate unified database decision; add parity and migration suites before offering PostgreSQL.

Title: Money stored as floating point
Description: STATIC: invoice, payment, ledger, cost and payroll amounts use Float and JS number; local rounding reduces but does not eliminate accumulation or allocation divergence.
Impact: Paisa discrepancies, reconciliation drift and inconsistent exports.
Likelihood: High at volume or edge values
Recommended fix: Choose integer minor units or validated Decimal across API/database/calculations; version conversion and reconcile historical totals before migration.

Title: Logical references lack database foreign keys
Description: STATIC: batch/catalogue/production/warehouse/QC/workflow/WIP/hold references and provider ControlRecord company/ControlAudit record links include plain scalar IDs without relations.
Impact: Orphans and invalid cross-domain links after concurrent edits/imports; provider records can refer to nonexistent companies.
Likelihood: Medium; live orphans UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Classify polymorphic versus concrete links; add validated relations and appropriate restrict/set-null policies after orphan inventory and controlled repair migration.

Title: Missing domain check and uniqueness constraints
Description: STATIC: status/type strings, financial signs and debit/credit exclusivity rely on code; singleton settings and staff/shift/day assignment uniqueness are not database-enforced.
Impact: Invalid states, duplicate settings and double assignments bypass application-only validation.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Define domain state machines and database constraints with migration preflight; add deterministic singleton and composite keys appropriate to business rules.

Title: Indexes missing for common filters and joins
Description: STATIC: multiple date/customer/status/invoice/entry/session/audit/warehouse/provider action access paths lack matching indexes; existing stock and customer-ledger indexes are acknowledged.
Impact: Increasing full scans and lock time as tenant history grows.
Likelihood: High at scale; timings UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Capture representative query plans, add only justified composite indexes and measure read/write costs in both supported storage profiles.

Title: Cascades can erase financial and audit history
Description: STATIC: invoice/payment/item, customer-ledger, staff-payroll and company-action cascades exist. This does not prove an exposed destructive HTTP path; legacy billing deletion is guarded.
Impact: Administrative or future deletes may remove retained accounting and action evidence.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Adopt retention-aware soft deletion and restrict protected history; define explicit archival/erasure procedures and test all graph deletions.

Title: Migration recovery and populated upgrades unproven
Description: STATIC/GAP: table rebuilds disable foreign keys and drop old tables; historical author/default-company rewrites exist; no tested downgrade or backup/forward-repair procedure evidenced.
Impact: Failed or semantically wrong migration can lose attribution/data or strand a tenant.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Review every transfer column and rewrite, rehearse populated upgrades and interruption recovery, take consistent verified backups and define forward-repair/restore gates.

Title: Time semantics mix UTC dates and host-local operations
Description: STATIC: date-only values combine with local clock; Tally formatting/day bounds, provider metric bucketing and summary queries use host timezone; mill timezone is not a consistent domain type.
Impact: Different servers produce different financial cutoffs, daily totals and event ordering.
Likelihood: High near day boundaries
Recommended fix: Model business date separately from UTC instant with explicit tenant IANA timezone; centralize conversions and date intervals including DST/non-IST tenants.

Title: Tracked database journal and packaged DB contamination risk
Description: STATIC: provider admin.db-journal is tracked with pre-existing AD worktree status; desktop bootstrap can copy packaged dev.db if present. Contents were not extracted.
Impact: Database fragments or customer/bootstrap records can enter source history or distributable images.
Likelihood: Medium; actual artifact content UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Exclude runtime databases/journals from source and build contexts, inspect historical/artifact exposure securely, initialize new installations only through audited migrations/bootstrap.

Title: ValidationPipe does not validate inline and any bodies
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610122122_P0_Safety): the six costing write routes now use DTOs, leaving 38 untyped bodies (commerce 18, inventory 5, workflows 5, job work 4, auth 2, billing 2, storefront 1, production 1). Earlier finding: STATIC: global whitelist/forbid/transform is configured, but many commerce/costing/inventory/provider/workflow handlers use inline shapes or any with manual partial validation; missing metadata bypasses DTO guarantees.
Impact: Unknown fields, malformed dates/numbers, invalid transitions and inconsistent errors reach services.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Define runtime DTO contracts for every request/query/response, strict nested transformation and domain validation; retain transaction-level invariants.

Title: Provider company/license mass assignment
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT: company create, license and sync routes take DTOs (companies.dto.ts) and write only allowlisted fields; companies.http.spec.ts drives malformed, extra-field and rollback cases over real HTTP. Earlier finding: STATIC: creation and license update spread caller-controlled data into Prisma rather than an explicit field allowlist and transition command.
Impact: Unauthorized scalar/nested mutation and invalid licensing state; extra UI details also cause Prisma errors.
Likelihood: High with SEC-001
Recommended fix: Introduce scoped creation/license command DTOs with explicit mapping, allowed transitions, version checks and transactional audit; reject unknown fields.

Title: Environment not comprehensively validated at startup
Description: STATIC: no unified boot schema for URLs, secrets, IDs, SMTP, sync or DB profile; bootstrap errors are caught instead of preventing unusable first startup.
Impact: Misconfigured production starts partially, fails later or silently uses unsafe defaults.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Create separate typed provider/tenant/agent configuration contracts with fail-fast required settings and explicit disabled optional integrations; validate launchers against them.

Title: Provider remote actions claim completion before execution
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT: unknown actions return 400 and unsupported ones 503 with nothing recorded; only TOGGLE_MAINTENANCE writes, in one transaction with its record, and it is labelled as unconfirmed by the tenant. Earlier finding: STATIC: RemoteAction is created EXECUTED/completed before local status changes; no authenticated tenant delivery/acknowledgment; maintenance toggle is not idempotent.
Impact: Operators believe tenant maintenance/migration/reactivation succeeded when no tenant action ran; retries invert maintenance.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Model requested/authorized/dispatched/acknowledged/completed/failed states, signed nonce-bound commands, tenant binding, durable delivery and idempotent desired-state actions.

Title: Migration endpoint blocks request process and lacks safe orchestration
Description: STATIC: execSync invokes unqualified npx prisma migrate deploy from request/boot paths without proven schema/cwd selection, distributed lock, restore gate or command audit; tenant JWT plus provider header are both required.
Impact: Event loop blocking, wrong-schema/failed migrations and unsafe concurrent upgrades.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Move migration execution to a dedicated signed deployment worker with explicit artifact/schema, locks, compatibility checks, backup verification, timeout and auditable outcomes.

Title: Telemetry transport uses wrong endpoint and no delivery contract
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 17 OCT: explicit ADMIN_API_URL and COMPANY_ID now gate all sync work; endpoint validation, HTTPS outside local development, redirect rejection, a 10-second request/body deadline, redacted failure logs and per-process overlap protection have regression coverage. All 77 sync tests pass; 27 new transport cases failed before the fix. Tenant authentication, durable delivery, backoff, payload-size limits and acknowledgement remain open; the schedule is still hourly. Earlier finding: STATIC: tenant sync hardcodes loopback admin URL, demo company fallback, unauthenticated fetch without timeout/outbox; configured ADMIN_API_URL/heartbeat interval are unused.
Impact: Heartbeat fails in containers or attributes the wrong company; requests may hang and license state remains stale.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Implement validated per-deployment endpoint/identity, authenticated schema-versioned payload, bounded timeouts, retries/backoff, durable deduplication and observable delivery status.

Title: API contracts and errors are inconsistent
Description: STATIC: mixed success/error shapes, raw service Error and controller false-result paths, parseInt coercions, duplicate verb decorators and no explicit API version contract.
Impact: Clients misinterpret failures as successes; integration evolution breaks callers.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Publish versioned OpenAPI contracts with strict parse pipes and stable typed errors/correlation IDs; replace ambiguous verbs and maintain compatibility tests.

Title: Mutation retries lack consistent idempotency and uniqueness
Description: STATIC: core workflows require requestKey, but many commerce, receipt, jobwork, costing and payroll writes do not; Date.now-based references and count-then-write quotas lack robust concurrent uniqueness policy.
Impact: Duplicate financial/stock writes, numbering collisions or quota overshoot under double submits/retries.
Likelihood: High with networks/concurrency
Recommended fix: Define scoped idempotency records with normalized payload hash and unique keys, transactional number allocation and conflict/replay semantics across all critical writes.

Title: Customer deactivation maps false to null
Description: STATIC: updateCustomer uses body[key] or null, turning active=false into null for a nonnullable boolean field.
Impact: Customer deactivation fails and returns database error.
Likelihood: High when used
Recommended fix: Use explicit field presence and typed boolean mapping, preserving false/zero; cover partial update semantics.

Title: Costing can accept caller-controlled category and arithmetic
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610122122_P0_Safety): all six costing write routes take validated DTOs; electricity, labour and packaging totals are computed on the server and a total, category or author sent by the caller is rejected; the one-entry-per-day check runs inside the posting transaction; zero values are kept on update. Whether electricity cost should multiply by the number of shifts is the existing formula and needs confirmation from the mill. Earlier finding: STATIC: spread order allows category override; component totals/rates are caller-controlled; truthy checks omit zero updates; duplicate existence check is outside atomic unique enforcement.
Impact: Incorrect operating costs and duplicate expense categories corrupt profitability.
Likelihood: High for malformed inputs
Recommended fix: Model typed costing commands per category, derive totals from validated quantities/rates, permit valid zeros and enforce composite business keys transactionally.

Title: Invoice verification does not prove stored record integrity
Description: STATIC: public verification returns stored hash/status rather than recomputing a canonical immutable issuer/buyer/items snapshot; hash coverage and mutation detection are incomplete.
Impact: Users may treat a verification response as cryptographic proof beyond what is implemented.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Define canonical versioned invoice snapshots and signed digest verification with key lifecycle; expose minimum public fields and validate tamper detection.

Title: Broad ledger reconciliation increases mutation scope
Description: RAISED TO P1 on 12 OCT: three stock passes, two lot passes, finance, valuation and two closed-period snapshots run on every write, so cost grows with total history. Earlier finding: STATIC: stockTransaction performs stock/lot/finance reconciliation and closed snapshots across growing record sets, making small mutations depend on broad history scans and long SQLite transactions.
Impact: Lock contention and timeouts increase with history; recovery and unrelated error coupling become harder.
Likelihood: High at scale
Recommended fix: Move to transactionally appended domain postings with bounded projections, explicit reconciliation jobs/checkpoints and invariant checks; preserve closed-period immutability.

Title: Order amendment uses a different tax rounding formula
Description: REPRODUCED: three lines of quantity 1, rate 0.10, GST 5% total 0.33 in canonical invoice arithmetic but 0.32 in amendment arithmetic.
Impact: Amended orders and resulting invoices disagree by paise; larger repeated differences affect reconciliation.
Likelihood: High for affected values
Recommended fix: Use one versioned financial calculation library across order/create/amend/invoice/export, backed by approved line/document rounding and regression properties.

Title: Discount allocation has no residual reconciliation
Description: STATIC: document discount is distributed proportionally and rounded per line without allocating residual paise; tax bases can disagree with document-level discounted subtotal.
Impact: GST/taxable value and total disagreement for small or uneven lines.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Allocate discounts in integer minor units with deterministic remainder distribution, prove conservation and snapshot calculation policy version.

Title: Payment retry identity is incomplete
Description: STATIC: optional request identity is stored in nonunique Payment.reference; duplicate comparison primarily checks amount and does not prove method/date/invoice payload equality.
Impact: Duplicate or mismatched receipts and ambiguous replay results under concurrent requests.
Likelihood: Medium to high
Recommended fix: Use a dedicated unique scoped idempotency record with canonical full payment fingerprint and immutable reversal entries; reconcile cash against party allocations.

Title: License lifecycle can override suspension
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT: the tenant validates the complete provider response before writing and an explicit SUSPENDED status wins over expiry and grace dates (admin-sync.service.spec.ts, 49 tests). Remaining nuance: a provider-set GRACE_PERIOD with a future expiry is recomputed as ACTIVE. Earlier finding: STATIC: tenant sync recalculates status from expiry/grace even when provider status is suspended; grace defaults differ and expected pricing/grace fields are omitted by provider response.
Impact: Suspended tenants can appear active; expiry behavior diverges between planes.
Likelihood: High when transitions overlap
Recommended fix: Define a shared authoritative transition table and signed license envelope; suspension/maintenance precedence, explicit grace policy and monotonic versions must be tested.

Title: License and module enforcement exists mainly in UI
Description: STATIC: suspended/maintenance/allowedModules/document quota state is not enforced across tenant API writes; cached UI overlays are bypassable by direct API calls.
Impact: Licensing controls do not govern actual service access; suspended operations continue.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Implement server-side entitlement policy with explicit allowed emergency/read actions, signed cached license state and documented offline/grace behavior.

Title: User machine and monthly-document quotas are unreliable
Description: PARTIALLY CORRECTED 17 OCT: sync now counts retained Invoice rows directly, including voided invoices, instead of estimating from Outward rows. The counter remains lifetime usage, not a billable-period count or quota enforcement. User/machine quota defects remain open. Earlier finding: STATIC: maxUsers check is on disabled signup while admin user creation bypasses it; machine count/create races; document count uses lifetime outward approximation rather than monthly quota enforcement.
Impact: Paid-plan restrictions can be exceeded or incorrectly reported.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Define quota dimensions/period/reset rules; enforce atomically at canonical creation endpoints with audited exceptions and correct telemetry counters.

Title: Weighbridge parser still accepts invalid units and trailing garbage
Description: REPRODUCED FINAL: original lb/g/sign/ERR42 cases were corrected externally; ST,GS,+100oz still becomes stable 100 kg, S S 1000 xyz becomes stable 1000 kg, trailing garbage is accepted, and moisture 12garbage becomes 12%. Prefix regexes do not validate the complete frame.
Impact: Wrong incoming weights directly affect stock and supplier bills.
Likelihood: High for supported malformed/unit variants
Recommended fix: Implement complete manufacturer-specific frame grammars with checksum/status validation, explicit supported unit conversion, strict moisture parsing and captured-device certification cases.

Title: Slip verification remains incomplete and replayable
Description: REPRODUCED FINAL: externally added checks now reject altered finalBillableKg, but altered excessMoisturePercent/antiFraudSeal still verify and a January-dated signed slip is accepted. Signature comparison is ordinary equality and no replay state exists.
Impact: Authenticated-looking slips can carry altered billing values or be replayed.
Likelihood: High if used for financial acceptance
Recommended fix: Sign a canonical full event or recompute all derived values on verification; use timing-safe comparison, device key rotation, monotonic sequence/nonce and timestamp replay window.

Title: Mill weight and loss rules lack signed-off complete model
Description: STATIC/GAP: moisture example passes but universal mill rule is unverified; fixed 60 kg bag conversion, explicit invisible-loss accounting, cone/core/box tare and Autoconer billing are incomplete or absent. Final production source now allows a symmetric 2% mass tolerance; see BIZ-015.
Impact: Commercial quantity and yield calculations may not match actual mill contracts or machine processes.
Likelihood: Unknown until domain signoff
Recommended fix: Obtain mill-approved quantity/tare/moisture/loss policies, model named units and tolerances, parameterize contractual rules and validate real approved examples before production billing.

Title: GST compliance model is incomplete
Description: STATIC/GAP: state comparison uses normalized display strings with Tamil Nadu fallbacks; HSN/place-of-supply/TCS and IRP schema lifecycle are not complete; applicable rates/thresholds need tax-owner verification.
Impact: Wrong interstate split or legally incomplete invoices for some transactions.
Likelihood: Medium; legal applicability UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Define tax jurisdiction codes, place-of-supply decision rules and effective-dated tax profiles with qualified tax review; implement IRP/HSN/TCS requirements applicable to customers.

Title: Public orders reserve stock without sufficient lifecycle protection
Description: STATIC: anonymous storefront creates confirmed reservations without an expiring pending/verified lifecycle and consistent request deduplication.
Impact: Stock can be exhausted by abandoned or abusive orders; retries create duplicates.
Likelihood: High on public exposure
Recommended fix: Model verified pending orders, reservation TTL/release jobs and idempotent checkout; apply abuse budgets and audit conversion/cancellation.

Title: Uninvoiced dispatch risk uses invented rate and incomplete status logic
Description: STATIC: risk uses fixed rate 260 and only no-invoice filtering; void-only and partially invoiced fulfilments are not accurately valued.
Impact: Misleading receivables dashboard and missed collections.
Likelihood: High when those cases occur
Recommended fix: Compute outstanding quantity from valid invoice/credit/void links and approved order prices; label unknown valuation instead of substituting a rate.

Title: Payroll is a manual arithmetic record without complete posting lifecycle
Description: STATIC/GAP: basic plus overtime minus deductions is recomputed, but paid state is not linked to a verified payment journey; attendance/shift-derived amounts and complete statutory rules are not implemented.
Impact: Payroll can be marked paid without financial reconciliation; attendance expectations unmet.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Define approval/post/payment/reversal lifecycle and attendance sources, compute approved rates/rounding centrally and reconcile bank/cash postings with explicit policy scope.

Title: Provider shared master key exposed to browser code/storage
Description: PARTIALLY CORRECTED EXTERNALLY at 54c5fe9: the committed fallback key and loopback URL are gone; the portal still authenticates with one shared key read from browser storage. Earlier finding: STATIC FINAL: authFetch was added externally and now sends Authorization, but obtains shared key from localStorage or VITE_ADMIN_API_KEY with a committed fallback. A Vite-provided secret is embedded in browser output. There is still no named-user login/session flow and API base remains loopback HTTP.
Impact: Provider portal cannot operate securely after bypass removal.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Replace browser master-key distribution with provider per-user authenticated sessions and server-held service credentials; remove build-time key injection, rotate potentially bundled keys, configure relative HTTPS API routing.

Title: Provider portal uses fabricated tenants and records on failures
Description: STATIC: DEMO_TENANTS/DEMO_RECORDS and sample activity appear in normal app paths; failed or empty API responses can retain/replace real data with demonstration rows.
Impact: Operators see false companies, payments and operations as real; production no-mock invariant fails.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Remove production fallback datasets; use explicit loading/empty/error/stale states with real provenance, and isolate demos in an excluded standalone build.

Title: Provider controls simulate successful operations
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 15 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610152245_Cleanup): the provider console terminal used to print fabricated health, backup ('Backup created successfully') and weighbridge results. It now prints only /health, /status and /control/database responses or an explicit failure, and states that backup, weighbridge, deploy and unknown commands did not run (App.test.tsx). Other simulated provider controls, such as CI/CD (INT-008), remain. Earlier finding: STATIC: ping returns random latency, terminal/AI return canned outcomes, backup claims success without work, and payment verification changes local state without gateway reconciliation.
Evidence: apps/admin-web/src/App.tsx; handleTestPing; handleRunTerminalCommand; handleRunAiAgent; payment handlers
Impact: False backup/deployment/payment assurance can cause data loss or financial decisions based on nonexistent actions.
Likelihood: High

Title: Provider release creation calls nonexistent API route
Description: STATIC: UI posts /cicd/releases while controller declares POST /cicd/build; GET releases exists.
Impact: Release creation fails even before replacing simulated pipeline.
Likelihood: High

Title: Reactivation payload and timing do not match backend
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 15 OCT: the renewal form sends fields the DTO accepts, blocks duplicate submits and no longer promises one-minute reactivation. Tenant confirmation is still absent (SEP-002). Title: Client navigation trusts stale stored role and lacks route guards
Description: STATIC: user object loads from localStorage without initial authoritative me refresh; navigation filters do not guard render branches/direct history events. API JWT role lookup remains a real server-side control.
Impact: Disallowed screens/actions appear; revoked/changed roles remain misleading until API errors.
Likelihood: High

Title: Forms do not consistently prevent duplicate submits or surface query errors
Description: STATIC: CommerceDesk actions lack uniform busy/disabled state and role policy; several data=[] fallbacks hide request failures as empty; partial client validation diverges from API.
Impact: Duplicate requests, hidden failures and confusing unauthorized actions.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Use shared form contracts and mutation state with idempotency keys, pending guards, field-level/server error display and distinct empty/error/loading states.

Title: Book-Ellam registers are incomplete and mis-mapped
Description: STATIC: DAYBOOK has no populated mapping; MACHINES reads nonexistent production fields and uses fixed yarn/machine labels; ledger uses customer balances rather than entries; stock excludes cotton/yarn.
Impact: Six-register promise is not met and operational rows/totals are wrong or missing.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Define six typed register contracts backed by canonical sources, shared date/search/pagination and cross-register identifiers; eliminate fabricated labels and reconcile totals.

Title: Book-Ellam dates loading and search conceal incomplete data
Description: STATIC: receipt createdAt can override effective date; errors are swallowed for several queries, loading watches only inward, and client search covers only loaded/mis-mapped records.
Impact: Backdated entries appear on wrong days; users assume incomplete searches are exhaustive.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Use business-date fields, explicit multi-source loading/error state and server-side exhaustive search with result counts and pagination.

Title: Displayed linear barcode is not Code128
Description: STATIC: SimpleSVGBarcode derives arbitrary bars from character codes with no standard start/checksum/stop encoding; QR uses an actual QR library.
Impact: Printed one-dimensional labels may not scan, interrupting traceability.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Use a maintained standards-compliant encoder with quiet zones/module size and device-tested label templates; preserve stable identifiers and audited reprints.

Title: Hindi missing and most UI strings not externalized
Description: STATIC: shared i18n and shell support English/Tamil only; large hardcoded English surfaces remain; no complete Hindi resources.
Impact: Promised multilingual operation and local staff usability are incomplete.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Centralize catalogs/pluralization/number/date formatters, add reviewed Tamil/Hindi translations and missing-key CI checks.

Title: Language preference promises retry that does not exist
Description: STATIC: user toggle calls ADMIN-only settings endpoint and failure toast promises save after reconnect, but no queued retry exists.
Impact: Ordinary staff cannot persist preference and receive a false success expectation.
Likelihood: High for non-admin users
Recommended fix: Store language as per-user preference with authorized endpoint or explicit local-only semantics; implement actual retry if promised.

Title: Provider and marketing lack equivalent error containment
Description: STATIC: tenant error boundaries exist; provider/marketing entrypoints have no equivalent root recovery boundary and many network errors are replaced by fallbacks.
Impact: Uncaught render errors can blank the page or mask failures with fake state.
Likelihood: Medium

Title: Marketing contact form does not submit leads
Description: STATIC: submit prevents default and marks contactSent locally; no backend delivery/persistence is called.
Impact: Prospective customer inquiries are silently lost while UI indicates submission.
Likelihood: High when used
Recommended fix: Implement consent-aware validated lead intake with abuse control, durable storage/delivery acknowledgment and clear failure state.

Title: Accessibility and low-end-device acceptance incomplete
Description: GAP: no full keyboard/screen-reader/contrast/touch matrix or real low-end GPU/print verification was executed. Existing reduced-motion, visibility pause and fallback code are positive evidence, not certification.
Impact: Keyboard/focus/visual/performance barriers may block factory staff; unknown accessibility defects remain.

Title: Dormant legacy financial/demo source remains alongside canonical workflows
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT with UI-020: the unreachable Billing, Payments and InvoiceGenerator sources are deleted. Earlier finding: STATIC: legacy Billing/Payments and the InvoiceGenerator state store retain persisted/demo data and older calculations; not all are reachable from current App imports. The active Store.tsx page uses real commerce APIs and must not be mislabeled a mock store. Active provider fallback defects are logged separately.

Title: Tally exports void invoices and internal payment movements
Description: STATIC: invoice/payment export has only date filtering; no VOID exclusion or distinction between cash receipts, allocations, allocation reversals and negative reversals; negative amounts can produce double-minus XML text.
Impact: Duplicate or invalid cash postings and overstated sales when imported into accounting.
Likelihood: High on affected records
Recommended fix: Export canonical posted accounting events with typed voucher/reversal mapping, invariant-balanced entries and an immutable export manifest; validate against a real Tally test company.

Title: Tally mapping delivery and acknowledgment incomplete
Description: STATIC: fixed sales/tax/bank ledger names ignore configured GST/item mapping; Create vouchers lack a stable integration identity; no transport/import acknowledgment parser; end-date midnight can omit later transactions; Purchase intentionally rejects.
Impact: Wrong ledgers, duplicate reimports, missed dates and no proof Tally accepted vouchers.
Likelihood: High when relied upon
Recommended fix: Add configured masters/ledger/tax mappings, voucher identity and import response/error reconciliation; use explicit inclusive business-date ranges and approved purchase-bill source.

Title: GST IRP and e-way-bill lifecycles absent
Description: STATIC/GAP: no real backend IRN authentication/generation/cancellation or e-way generation/extension/cancel/Part-B workflow found; UI affordances do not prove integrations.
Impact: Customers cannot rely on displayed controls for statutory document generation.
Likelihood: Certain implementation gap; applicability UNVERIFIED
Recommended fix: Implement provider-specific adapters with credentials, schema versioning, idempotent request/ack storage, retries and reconciliation; complete sandbox-to-production certification.

Title: Payment gateway and verified webhooks absent
Description: STATIC/GAP: no inbound Razorpay/Stripe signature/raw-body/replay/idempotency/reconciliation flow found; provider payment verification is local UI state.
Impact: Payment statuses can be asserted without settlement evidence; duplicate/lost webhook events cannot reconcile ledgers.
Likelihood: Certain feature gap
Recommended fix: Implement selected gateway contract with signature verification over raw bytes, account/event binding, durable inbox, idempotent postings, retries/DLQ and settlement reconciliation.

Title: WhatsApp is a link builder and SMS is missing
Description: STATIC: collection service produces wa.me text link, not provider delivery; no approved template IDs, opt-out, delivery callbacks or SMS adapter; audit actor is generic.
Impact: Collection reminders have no trustworthy delivery state, preference enforcement or attribution.
Likelihood: High if presented as automated messaging
Recommended fix: Distinguish compose-link feature from managed messaging; implement consent/preferences, approved templates, authenticated callbacks and durable delivery state only if required.

Title: Weighbridge agent production entrypoint is simulation
Description: STILL OPEN 15 OCT: src/index.ts exports runAgentSimulation with a fixed sample frame; there is no serial capture. Earlier finding: STATIC: start runs runAgentSimulation with fixed frames/device/vendor/secret; no real serial listener, reconnect/offline durable buffering or server ingestion contract is implemented.
Impact: No reliable live weight capture; demo readings may be mistaken for hardware data.
Likelihood: High if agent deployed
Recommended fix: Build a device-authenticated serial adapter with protocol-specific parser, stable-reading criteria, durable local queue, sequence deduplication and offline/reconnect recovery; exclude simulator from shipped entrypoint.

Title: Printer integration lacks safe transport and reprint controls
Description: STATIC: TSPL/ZPL strings interpolate unescaped identifiers and are only generated; no certified driver/transport, retry status or audited reprint lifecycle found.
Impact: Malformed/hostile identifiers alter printer commands; labels may silently fail or duplicate.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Define restricted template encoding, validated printer transport profiles and spool job states; authenticate reprints and retain original label identity/sequence.

Title: Provider CI/CD and cloud deployment APIs fabricate execution
Description: STATIC: service initializes sample releases/deployments/logs, generates random checksum-like values and writes appVersion/migration status/success without actual build, cloud deployment or health verification.
Impact: False release/rollback/health evidence and incorrect fleet version records.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Replace simulations with persisted signed artifact provenance and authorized deployment workers; report only verified stage outcomes, checksums, migration versions and tenant health acknowledgments.

Title: Email delivery lacks durable failure and preference handling
Description: STATIC: SMTP is optional/no-op when unset, no outbox/bounce/retry handling, hardcoded sender identity, inconsistent emailNotifications use, and unescaped user/device fields in HTML templates.
Impact: Silent delivery failures, misleading notification settings and email content injection.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Validate SMTP/TLS/sender configuration, escape template values, honor preferences, queue notifications with deduplication and process authenticated delivery/bounce events.

Title: Daily summary schedule and aggregation are wrong
Description: STATIC: cron 29 23 UTC runs 04:59 IST rather than documented 23:59 IST; findFirst production undercounts multiple runs; no sent-event uniqueness or distributed lease.
Impact: Incomplete summaries arrive on the wrong day and duplicate on replicas; failures are not reliably recovered.
Likelihood: High when enabled
Recommended fix: Schedule by explicit tenant timezone, aggregate all effective-date production/cost records, use a unique tenant/date notification job with safe retries.

Title: Tenant settings expose provider-only license and pricing state
Description: STATIC: settings read returns provider-managed flags/plan/pricing/license/quota fields to tenant viewers; tenant UI contains provider-derived plan controls/status fields. Update allowlist does exclude provider fields, a positive boundary.
Impact: User-required provider-only invisibility is violated even where writes are blocked.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Separate internal entitlement cache from tenant-visible company settings with explicit DTOs; expose only approved operational availability messages and no provider pricing/control metadata.

Title: Telemetry identity and payload are not tenant-bound
Description: STATIC: metrics accepts arbitrary companyId under provider-wide authority, tenant does not send its issued key, additionalMetrics accepts arbitrary JSON and replay timestamps/nonces are absent.
Impact: Cross-company telemetry poisoning and potentially license response confusion; arbitrary payload can leak business data to provider.
Likelihood: High after shared-key compromise; per-tenant binding absent
Recommended fix: Use per-tenant authenticated service identities bound server-side to company, signed schema allowlist and nonce/sequence; explicitly approve aggregate usage fields and reject business rows/freeform data.

Title: Plane boundaries are not enforced by build policy
Description: STATIC/GAP: frontend import graph has separate app entries, but tenant exposes provider-derived settings and there is no enforced import ownership/artifact gate. Provider prebuild was changed externally to generate admin Prisma; shared PDF dependency is intentional sharing, not proof of tenant-data access.
Impact: Future changes can accidentally ship opposite-plane code; provider build is coupled to tenant persistence tooling.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Define allowed shared packages/contracts and prohibit cross-plane application/database imports with static rules and CI bundle manifests; split provider build prerequisites.

Title: Physical tenant isolation not proven by deployment evidence
Description: GAP: separate Prisma clients/DB environment names and named volumes support intended topology; no two-real-tenant HTTP/DB/backup/network isolation test or actual cloud IAM inventory was available. Fixed container names and one template do not provision independent customer fleets.
Impact: Misprovisioning could connect customers to the same DB/volume/credentials despite correct source intent.
Likelihood: Unknown
Recommended fix: Provision unique per-tenant DB/volumes/service identities/networks/secrets with ownership assertions and fail-closed startup; prove isolation across APIs, jobs, backups and restore using two deployments.

Title: Unbounded lists N+1 aggregation and truncated UI histories
Description: STATIC: item/customer list performs per-record aggregate queries; workflow overview loads many full tables; several screens cap results without cursor continuation and filter on client.
Impact: Latency/memory grow with history, while capped screens silently hide older records.
Likelihood: High at scale
Recommended fix: Introduce cursor/filter/sort contracts, batch aggregate queries, server counts/search and incremental UI loading; virtualize large visible lists where measured necessary.

Title: Large tenant JavaScript chunks
Description: MEASURED: production build includes approximately 894 kB OrbitControls/Three chunk and 786 kB entry, plus PDF/chart/canvas chunks; some lazy loading exists. Actual device load/FPS and cache behavior were not measured.
Impact: Slow first interaction and expensive 3D/export workloads on factory devices.
Likelihood: Medium to high on low-end hardware
Recommended fix: Profile route-level transferred/executed code, split expensive feature boundaries and imports, set bundle/device budgets and retain accessible lightweight 3D alternative.

Title: Broad invalidation and per-request session writes add load
Description: STATIC: client invalidates broadly for POST operations including nonmutating actions; JWT validation updates session activity on each request; blanket no-store blocks selective caching; Redis config has no active cache/queue service role.
Impact: Repeated refetches and SQLite writes amplify otherwise read-heavy workflows.
Likelihood: High at scale
Recommended fix: Use scoped mutation invalidation, bounded/coalesced session activity updates and deliberate private/static caching policies; add cache only with measured consistency/invalidation rules.

Title: No measured capacity or cost baseline
Description: GAP: no executed target-size load/stress/soak profile, query p95/p99, event-loop lag, contention test, queue-depth limit or actual infrastructure bill was available; 10x/100x and over-provisioning claims cannot be made.
Evidence: tests/CI; deployment manifests; audit verification log
Impact: Capacity and cost failure thresholds unknown before customer growth.
Likelihood: Unknown
Recommended fix: Define representative tenant profiles and SLOs; run isolated realistic load/soak experiments and collect query/CPU/memory/queue/cost metrics, then size limits from evidence.

Title: Container build recipes reference missing inputs/scripts
Description: STILL OPEN 15 OCT: all five Dockerfiles still COPY a root tsconfig.json that does not exist, and Dockerfile.tenant-api still runs db:generate. Earlier finding: STATIC FINAL: API Dockerfiles COPY root tsconfig.json which does not exist; tenant invokes nonexistent db:generate workspace script; provider requires PDF workspace omitted from initial manifest installation. Provider prebuild was corrected externally to generate admin Prisma. Docker build itself was not run.
Impact: Documented production images cannot be built reproducibly from the reviewed tree.
Likelihood: High/certain missing inputs
Recommended fix: Create dependency-complete multi-stage builds using actual workspace scripts/configs; add clean-context image build and boot smoke tests for every plane.

Title: Container migration failures are swallowed
Description: RESOLVED EXTERNALLY at 54c5fe9: both entrypoints run migrate deploy under set -e without swallowing failure and require DATABASE_URL. Earlier finding: STATIC: entrypoint migration failure is followed by echo and normal server startup; licensing schema drift makes this especially hazardous.
Impact: App starts against incompatible schema and can partially fail after being declared healthy.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Make migration failure fatal or run a gated deployment migration job with explicit compatible schema/readiness; never start an incompatible application.

Title: Image hygiene permissions and runtime parity unproven
Description: STATIC/GAP: no root .dockerignore excludes env/runtime DBs, broad COPY packages/apps, full dev node_modules copied, non-root SQLite directory ownership not established, floating images and Node versions differ across local/CI/container.
Impact: Secrets/data enter image contexts, oversized vulnerable runtime, unwritable DB volume or environment-only failures.
Likelihood: Medium to high
Recommended fix: Define minimal allowlisted build contexts, runtime-only dependency artifacts, non-root owned DB volumes, supported pinned runtime/image digests and provenance/SBOM checks.

Title: Deployment transport network and proxy controls incomplete
Description: STATIC/GAP: production example publishes APIs and uses HTTP; tenant joins provider network without egress policy; dev PostgreSQL/Redis are published with weak/default auth; nginx headers/TLS and proxy trust do not establish production protection.
Impact: Control-plane exposure, intercepted credentials and incorrect IP/rate-limit attribution; actual ingress TLS is UNVERIFIED.
Likelihood: High if templates used unchanged
Recommended fix: Define TLS ingress/mTLS where needed, isolated plane networks and least-privilege egress, private admin/DB ports, verified trusted proxies and consistent edge security headers.

Title: No proven automated backup restore or disaster recovery
Description: STATIC/GAP: autoBackup setting and provider terminal claims do not implement backups; no automated verified offsite encrypted snapshot/restore, RTO/RPO drill or recovery evidence found.
Impact: Tenant financial/operational data can be permanently lost; recovery time is unknown.
Likelihood: Unknown event likelihood; certain assurance gap
Recommended fix: Define per-tier RPO/RTO, consistent per-tenant encrypted backups with separately controlled retention, automatic integrity checks and scheduled restore/failover drills.

Title: Logging monitoring tracing and incident evidence incomplete
Description: STATIC/GAP: console logs include business payloads, no consistent structured redaction/correlation, central search/tracing/alerts/dashboard/runbook acceptance evidence; health UI substitutes inferred states.
Impact: Incidents are hard to detect and correlate; sensitive business data may leak through logs.
Likelihood: High during incident
Recommended fix: Implement structured redacted event logs, request/job correlation, metrics/traces, dependency SLO alerts and exercised runbooks; separate customer data from provider telemetry.

Title: Background work lacks durable queues and recovery semantics
Description: STATIC: hourly heartbeat/daily summary and remote actions have no persisted job leases, bounded retry/DLQ or crash recovery; horizontally scaled crons may duplicate work.
Impact: Lost or duplicate notifications/actions, overlapping work and unbounded stale state.
Likelihood: High across failures/replicas
Recommended fix: Introduce durable inbox/outbox and job state machines with idempotent handlers, leases, bounded retries, dead letters and operator replay controls.

Title: Linux provisioning script is incomplete and inconsistent
Description: STATIC: script writes env without required JWT/bootstrap, uses TENANT_SLUG rather than sync COMPANY_ID, assumes apt-get despite broader OS claims and does not implement a complete build/download/start lifecycle.
Impact: Provisioning fails or produces unusable/stale installation and missing license sync.
Likelihood: High if used
Recommended fix: Replace with idempotent versioned provisioning for explicitly supported OS targets, secret injection, artifact verification, migration/health gates and rollback tested in clean VMs.

Title: Desktop artifact diverges from current application and trusts external URLs
Description: STATIC/GAP: packaged backend/web-dist/schema and separate lockfile can be stale; Electron pinned 33; copied initial DB risk; arbitrary shell.openExternal schemes are not allowlisted and fallback localhost3000 may open another app.
Impact: Desktop users run a different security/data model; unsafe external navigation and unsupported runtime vulnerabilities.
Likelihood: Medium to high
Recommended fix: Generate desktop artifacts from the same release graph, migrate per-user data securely, update supported Electron, allowlist navigation/protocols and verify signed installers/auto-update policy.

Title: No real canary rollback or zero-downtime release proof
Description: GAP: provider UI declares deployment/rollback success without execution; no verified fleet rollout, release tag/artifact provenance, backward-compatible migration or rollback drill was available.
Impact: A bad release can affect many mills without reliable containment/recovery.
Likelihood: Unknown
Recommended fix: Implement staged per-tenant deployment rings with signed immutable artifacts, schema compatibility windows, readiness/SLI gates and exercised rollback/forward repair.

Title: HTTP integration tests fail before exercising routes
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit f158a40): both tenant HTTP suites run (2 suites, 19 tests passing) and npm run verify now includes them. Earlier finding: MEASURED: all five tenant HTTP tests fail during Prisma migration setup; repeating with elevated access gives the same schema-engine error. Native root cause is unresolved and distinct from proven SQL/schema drift.

Description: MEASURED: tenant API statements 14.39%, branches 9.9%; tenant web statements 18.4%; all existing selected tests pass but do not prove full coverage.
Impact: Critical service and UI regressions evade passing unit suites.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Prioritize production-importing invariant and transaction tests over shallow line metrics; set ratcheting domain coverage and risk-based required scenarios.

Title: Provider tests are too narrow and admin-web absent from normal test script
Description: MEASURED: initial provider API had 5 passing tests; final recheck has 11 passing tests in 3 suites after external guard regression additions. Provider web has 4 manually run tests and no package test script; copied provider e2e imports missing tenant auth setup. Broad control-plane coverage is still absent.
Impact: Most provider operations/security never receive meaningful CI exercise.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Create isolated provider DB/API/browser suites and wire them to the normal workspace/CI command; replace incorrect copied scaffolding.

Title: Security isolation and full business journey tests missing
Description: GAP: no executed complete role-by-route/two-tenant IDOR/security matrix or inward-to-production-to-dispatch-to-invoice-to-payment-reversal journey; unit mocked flows are not equivalent.
Impact: Cross-layer authorization, stock and financial defects remain unproven.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Build disposable two-deployment fixtures and real HTTP/browser journeys including direct denied calls, concurrency, rollback, recovery and signed external contracts.

Title: Lint and dependency findings do not block CI
Description: PARTIALLY CORRECTED EXTERNALLY at 54c5fe9: lint and audit steps no longer use continue-on-error, but the build is failing; see TEST-009. Earlier finding: STATIC: both lint jobs and npm audit use continue-on-error; audit found critical/high packages. Root verify omits HTTP suites and provider migration-diff gate; remote branch protection/manual override policy unknown.
Impact: Known security and quality failures can merge/release while CI appears successful.

Recommended fix: Make risk-reviewed security/quality checks and both migration/HTTP suites required, with explicit time-bound exception approval and auditable branch/release protection.

Title: No complete API contract integration and device certification suite
Description: PARTIALLY IMPROVED 17 OCT: root typecheck and CI verify now include customer API unit and HTTP test files. Six stale constructor/calculator/mock type errors were reproduced and fixed without widening production contracts; the expanded typecheck and changed-file lint pass. The full API suite passed 293 tests, and all 47 affected tests passed after final mock cleanup. Broader contract, sandbox and device acceptance remains open. Earlier finding: GAP: frontend/provider route mismatch, financial rounding divergence and simulated integrations have no generated contract/sandbox/device certification gate; some calculation tests duplicate formulas rather than import the implementation.
Impact: Tests can pass while production contracts/calculations/devices diverge.
Likelihood: High
Recommended fix: Generate typed contracts from runtime schemas, test production calculation modules directly, and add deterministic external sandbox/device protocol certification suites.

Title: Full dependency and production artifact assurance remains incomplete
Description: MEASURED/GAP: root and desktop npm trees were checked live; archived lockfiles are inventoried but not all audited; OS packages, browser binaries, container layers and final signed installer SBOMs not assessed.
Impact: Known or undisclosed vulnerable components outside npm audit may ship.
Likelihood: Unknown
Recommended fix: Define release scope, exclude archives, produce artifact SBOMs and scan every shipped dependency/image/runtime against current advisories with reachability and license review.

Title: Read-only audit cannot certify live data correctness or UX
Description: GAP: no production DB read snapshot, real mill signed examples, external credentials, live multi-tenant deployment, hardware or browser acceptance session was available; no live orphan/duplicate/ledger/PII counts or screen-by-screen success claim is justified.
Impact: Shipping decisions require evidence not obtainable from source and isolated tests alone.
Likelihood: Certain assurance gap
Recommended fix: Execute a controlled acceptance plan with authorized scrubbed snapshots, sandbox accounts, two deployments and devices; attach evidence for every currently UNVERIFIED gate.

Title: Costing update could block every posting and startup
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit b4bd048): PUT /costing/:id updated outside stockTransaction with no range check. A zero-amount entry is never journaled, so a MODIFIER could set it negative, after which reconcileFinance threw on every stockTransaction and in onModuleInit. Update and delete now validate every field and run inside stockTransaction; authorship comes from the session.
Impact: Any MODIFIER could stop all stock and finance writes and prevent the API from starting.
Likelihood: High before correction; closed in corrected source
Recommended fix: Keep the regression suite as a release gate; replace untyped costing bodies with DTOs under API-001 and compute component totals on the server under API-010.
Test to add: costing.service.spec.ts and p0-safety.e2e-spec.ts: cannot turn an unposted entry negative and take every posting down with it

Title: Startup reconciliation aborted boot on one invalid business record
Description: PARTIALLY RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit b4bd048): onModuleInit ran full reconciliation with no error handling, so any record breaking a ledger rule stopped the API from starting. Startup now tolerates business-rule failures, shows the reason to administrators at GET /status and names the offending record; schema and connectivity failures remain fatal. Postings still fail until the record is corrected, and whole-ledger reconciliation on every write remains (API-012).
Impact: Total outage, including sign-in and read access, from a single bad row.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Retire reconcile-on-write in favour of posting at the point of change plus a scheduled drift report (API-012).
Test to add: prisma.service.spec.ts: still starts when one business record breaks a ledger rule, and remembers why

Title: Document numbers are timestamps, not a compliant series
Description: STATIC: invoice, sales order, goods receipt, job-work challan and merge-batch numbers default to a prefix plus Date.now(). INV- plus 13 digits is 17 characters; numbers are not consecutive, not per financial year, and the caller may supply any number. Credit notes use a random UUID fragment and an invoice void posts a ledger credit with no document number. GST invoice rules call for a consecutive serial of at most 16 characters unique within the financial year; confirm applicability with the tax adviser.
Impact: Invoices may be non-compliant and cannot be reconciled by sequence; collisions surface only as unique-constraint errors.
Likelihood: Certain on every auto-numbered document
Recommended fix: Add a document-series table keyed by series and financial year, allocate the next number inside the posting transaction, keep numbers within 16 characters, number credit notes and voids from their own series, and stop accepting caller-supplied numbers except for controlled imports.

Title: Cost of goods sold and production reversals are missing from the ledger
Description: STATIC: an invoice linked to a dispatch creates no stock movement at invoice time and the dispatch issue of legacy yarn is offset to MANUFACTURING_CLEARING, so COST_OF_SALES is never debited for the main mill flow. Deleting a production hard-deletes its stock rows while PRODUCTION_COST and WIP journal entries remain, and its costing pre-check matches on an exact timestamp.
Impact: Gross margin is overstated and the trial balance keeps cost for production that no longer exists.
Likelihood: High on every mill dispatch and production deletion
Recommended fix: Post cost of sales when dispatched goods are invoiced; replace production deletion with a reversal document that reverses stock, WIP and journals together.

Title: Moisture deduction, waste sales and merged-batch cost never reach the accounts
Description: STATIC: the weighbridge receipt stores finalBillableKg and moistureDeductionKg only inside a JSON snapshot; linking the receipt to a supplier bill uses the full batch weight. Waste export records no revenue, GST or ledger entry and takes createdBy from the request body. Merged and recycled batches are created without unitCost, so their value drops out of stock valuation.
Impact: Suppliers are paid on undeducted weight, waste income is unrecorded and stock is undervalued after merges.
Likelihood: High wherever these flows are used
Recommended fix: Carry billable weight into the supplier bill under an approved contract rule, sell waste through the invoice path, and carry weighted cost through merge and recycle.

Title: Tax type and rate can be decided by caller-supplied text
Description: STATIC: seller and buyer state come from the request body before settings or the customer master; CGST/SGST versus IGST is chosen by comparing state names as text, so TN versus Tamil Nadu yields IGST. GST rate and HSN come from the invoice line with item fallback and HSN may be null; customer GSTIN is never validated and item GST rate is stored unchecked.
Impact: Wrong tax head or rate on issued invoices.
Likelihood: Medium; depends on data entry and direct API use
Recommended fix: Derive state from a validated GSTIN or a state-code master, take rate and HSN from the item master with an audited override, and reject invoices without HSN where required.

Title: Web calls routes and filters the API does not provide
Description: STATIC: Costing requests GET /production/history, which has no route; the error is swallowed, so cost per kg always shows 0 or No production. Date filters sent to GET /production and GET /costing/entries are ignored by controllers that take no query. Dead-code callers also target /costing/dashboard and /auth/signup.
Impact: Users see a wrong cost per kg and unfiltered lists while believing a filter applied.
Likelihood: Certain
Recommended fix: Generate the web client from the API OpenAPI description so drift fails the build; add the missing server-side filters and remove the non-existent call.

Title: Notifications read the retired billing endpoint and disagree on thresholds
Description: STATIC: the notification sync polls GET /billing/invoices with legacy field names while live invoicing is /commerce/invoices, so overdue alerts miss current invoices. The low-stock threshold default is 10 in App.tsx, 100 in the hook and 500 in Settings.
Impact: Missed overdue alerts and inconsistent low-stock warnings.

Title: Sensitive financial actions are open to the MODIFIER role
Description: STATIC: unlimited positive stock adjustments, supplier payments and refunds, valuation postings, customer receipts, purchase-order cancellation and quality-hold release have no administrator or finance gate. A raw role comparison in the workflows controller bypasses role normalisation.
Impact: Any data-entry user can create stock or move money in the books.
Likelihood: Medium

Title: Two React versions are installed and bundled; main fails its own verify script
Description: RESOLVED (commit c13cfaf), MEASURED 15 OCT: npm ls reports a single react@19.3.0 across the workspace. Earlier finding: MEASURED 12 OCT on 54c5fe9: apps/web pins react and react-dom 19.3.0 while the lockfile keeps 19.2.4 at the workspace root, where MUI and the testing library resolve it. A production vite build of apps/web contains both version strings in the entry chunk, so library hooks bind to a React that react-dom never drives. Component tests that use hooks fail with Cannot read properties of null (reading useState or useRef), including three in workspace.test.tsx, and tsc for apps/web reports 86 errors because the jest-dom matcher types are not registered for Vitest 5. All reproduce with the P0 branch stashed. CI now blocks on these steps. Whether the built app renders was not exercised in a browser.
Impact: The shipped web bundle is likely to fail at first render; no change can pass CI; real regressions hide behind an already failing build.
Likelihood: Certain for tests and type-check; likely for the built app
Recommended fix: Install exactly one react and react-dom version across every workspace (align the pins and regenerate the lockfile, or add a root override), import the Vitest entry of jest-dom so matcher types resolve, add a CI check that fails when more than one React copy is installed, and keep verify passing as a merge requirement.

Title: Symmetric mass tolerance permits stock creation and unposted loss
Description: STATIC FINAL: production accepts total yarn plus waste plus intermediate between 98% and 102% of input plus rounding allowance. Thus 100 kg input can pass with 102 kg output; under-consumption is not persisted as a distinct approved loss event. Contract authority for tolerance is unverified.
Impact: Mass can be created or disappear from explicit production accounting.
Likelihood: High at permitted boundary
Recommended fix: Model explicit measurement uncertainty and approved loss/gain events with domain-owner authorization; require conserved mass using named quantities and measured tolerances instead of symmetric unexplained allowance.

Title: Store estimate uses a separate floating tax formula
Description: STATIC: Store.tsx sums quantity × salePrice × (1 + gstRate/100) and formats only the total, while canonical invoice code rounds tax per line. Three separate 0.10 items at 18% estimate 0.35 versus canonical 0.36. Real browser/order roundtrip remains unverified.
Impact: Customers/staff can see an estimate inconsistent with canonical order/invoice amounts.
Likelihood: Medium at rounding boundaries
Recommended fix: Use the canonical typed pricing/rounding contract or a server quote endpoint for estimates; label and version quotes and recompute at posting.

Title: Database Studio exposes every table to any authenticated tenant role
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): scripts/database-studio.js is deleted; npm run db:studio starts Prisma Studio bound to 127.0.0.1 for development only. Earlier finding: STATIC: custom HTTP Studio checks only authContext, not ADMIN/provider permission; /api/table/:name runs SELECT * on every database table, including User/Session/settings/payroll. Browser category/role badges do not protect these endpoints.
Impact: A VIEWER can read password hashes, TOTP secrets, session IDs, personnel and unrestricted business rows when Studio is reachable.
Likelihood: High when tool is running and reachable
Recommended fix: Move database administration outside customer sessions into an operator-only service/network with explicit identity, MFA and table/field policy; use read-only credentials where possible and immutable audited access.

Title: Database Studio provides unrestricted raw SQL without write authorization
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): scripts/database-studio.js is deleted; npm run db:studio starts Prisma Studio bound to 127.0.0.1 for development only. Earlier finding: STATIC: POST /api/query passes request.query directly to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe after only a session check. No read-only SQL policy, independent read-only connection, role restriction, transaction/domain validation, audit or statement timeout exists. Actual destructive SQL was not executed.
Impact: Any authenticated role may bypass domain/RBAC/license/closed-period controls, read all data and potentially mutate data using supported SQL statements; exact native mutation behavior remains unexecuted.
Likelihood: High when tool is exposed
Recommended fix: Remove arbitrary SQL from tenant-facing services; design a separate privileged audited operator workflow with database-enforced read-only access for inspection and reviewed maintenance jobs for mutations.

Title: Studio alternate login bypasses TOTP and issues longer shared sessions
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): scripts/database-studio.js is deleted; npm run db:studio starts Prisma Studio bound to 127.0.0.1 for development only. Earlier finding: STATIC: /api/auth/login validates password only, creates the same Session model and signs a seven-day JWT with the tenant secret; it never checks isTotpEnabled. Tenant JwtStrategy accepts matching sessionId/sub without a distinct issuer/audience/factor-level contract.
Impact: An account protected by TOTP can obtain an authenticated session through the weaker alternate service; token scope/lifetime crosses application boundaries when secrets match.
Likelihood: High when Studio reachable
Recommended fix: Unify strong authentication and factor assurance or isolate operator identity completely; enforce audience/issuer/session purpose and MFA level in every verifier, remove fallback secrets and revoke old cross-purpose sessions.

Title: Studio binds all interfaces with permissive CORS and unbounded requests
Description: RESOLVED 12 OCT (branch commit 6cb945e): scripts/database-studio.js is deleted; npm run db:studio starts Prisma Studio bound to 127.0.0.1 for development only. Earlier finding: STATIC: custom server listens 0.0.0.0:5555, sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin *, accumulates login/query bodies without size limit, has no rate limiting/query resource budget and sets session cookie without Secure. It does not inherit Nest guards/Helmet/ValidationPipe/body limits.
Impact: Unexpected network exposure, brute force/memory/query exhaustion and weaker browser/transport protections on a privileged data service.
Likelihood: High if launched on shared host
Recommended fix: Restrict operator tooling to loopback/private authenticated access, explicit origins and HTTPS; enforce body/time/result/query limits and shared auth/rate policy, with production launch prohibition unless approved.

Title: Marketing site promises capabilities that are not built

Title: Weighbridge library silently defaults the moisture base to 8.5%
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610152245_Cleanup): the contract base is now required; a missing or invalid base throws RangeError and a slip without one does not verify (indicator-parsers.test.ts). Earlier finding: STATIC 15 OCT: AntiTamperEngine.calculateCottonMoisture(gross, tare, moisture, baseMoisture = 8.5) applies 8.5% when the caller omits the contract base, although its own comments and the moisture research say there is no universal base.
Impact: A missing contract value yields a plausible but wrong billable weight.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Make the contract base required, or return a pending-settlement result when it is absent, and test the omission.

Title: Label printer commands embed unescaped text
Description: RESOLVED 15 OCT (branch GokulSenthilkumar/202610152245_Cleanup): every label field passes through tsplText or zplText, which remove control characters and replace TSPL quotes and ZPL carets and tildes; hostile-name tests cover both formats. Earlier finding: STATIC 15 OCT: generateTsplCommand and generateZplCommand interpolate mill, supplier, lot and date strings into quoted printer commands without escaping quotes, carets or tildes.
Impact: A supplier name containing a quote can break the label or inject printer commands.
Likelihood: Medium
Recommended fix: Escape or reject control characters following TSPL and ZPL rules, and test with hostile names.
